brief_summary: Cross-section of a single stabilizer tower seated through a plate cutout onto a PCB. The stem sits in the housing bore and the wire leg (seen end-on) sits in the slot at the stem base. Three coral-filled slivers mark the three required clearances, each with a numbered coral callout: ① wire leg to stem slot (rattle; Norbauer's 0.3mm clearance figure), ② stem to housing bore (tick/scrape), ③ housing to plate cutout / PCB (clunk). Serif italic title 'three clearances · all required · all audible'.
data_sources: why-stabilizers-rattle-deep-dive.mdx § 'Tolerance stacking: three gaps that have to exist' — 'every sliding or rotating pair in it needs clearance: stem in housing bore, wire leg in the slot at the base of the stem, housing in its plate cutout or on the PCB'
